Brian Terwilliger Twigg The Battle for R.title: Brian Terwilliger Twigg The Battle for Reflections 2 (tournament report)

main.content:
'''Brian Terwilliger Twigg The Battle for Reflections 2 (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Brian Terwilliger]] posted on DeckTech on 31 December 2000 about [[December 2000 Clifton Park tournament]].[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2000-12-31-twigg-the-battle-for-reflections-2d1586/ twigg-the-battle-for-reflections-2], DeckTech (Brian "twigg" Terwilliger, 31 December 2000). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2000-12-31-twigg-the-battle-for-reflections-2d1586/ GitHub Pages]. Brian Terwilliger won a 25-player tournament at the Gamers Guild in Clifton Park, New York, in December 2000 with an EBO deck and Hunt Down Surprise, going 5–1 for 10 (+102) and losing only the last round to Chris Terwilliger. == Report info == * '''Author:''' [[Brian Terwilliger]] (byline: Brian "twigg" Terwilliger) * '''Published:''' 31 December 2000 (DeckTech) * '''Report title:''' ''Twigg The Battle for Reflections 2'' * '''Event:''' [[December 2000 Clifton Park tournament]] * '''Event date:''' December 2000 * '''Site:''' Gamers Guild, Clifton Park, NY * '''Players:''' 25 * '''Finish:''' 1st * '''Record:''' 5–1 * '''Points:''' 10 (+102) * '''Light deck:''' EBO, Baraguains, and Missles * '''Dark deck:''' [[Brian Terwilliger Twigg's Hunt Down Suprise|Hunt Down Surprise]] == Games == Games as the author describes them; margins are as stated in the report. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Round !! Opponent !! Author's deck !! Opponent's deck !! Result !! Margin |- | 1 || Todd Schnitzer || [[Light]] EBO, Baraguins and Missiles || Skum || Win || FW +31 |- | 2 || [[Jonny Chu]] || [[Dark]] [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down Surprise]] || X-Wing Swarm || Win || FW +19 |- | 3 || [[Arthur Wright]] || [[Light]] EBO, Baraguins and Missiles || [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down Duel]] || Win || FW +23 |- | 4 || [[Dan Sokol]] || [[Dark]] [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down Surprise]] || Y4 Mains || Win || FW +8 |- | 5 || [[Mike Panayotou]] || [[Light]] EBO, Baraguins and Missiles || Big Blue Space || Win || FW +31 |- | 6 || [[Chris Terwilliger]] || [[Dark]] [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down Surprise]] || Y4 Mains || Loss (report calls him 'Little Twigg' and 'chris'; side not stated, Dark inferred from his Vader/Emperor/Executor play) || FL −10 |} == Other results named in the report == * 10 (+75): [[Jonny Chu]] * 10 (+64): [[Chris Terwilliger]] * 8 (+45): [[Mike d'Amboise]] * 8 (+24): [[Joe Giannetti]] * 8 (+23): [[Matt Sokol]] * 8 (+22): [[Dan Sokol]] * 8 (+21): [[Martin Terwilliger]] * 8 (+12): [[Aaron Kingery]] == Original report == '''twigg-the-battle-for-reflections-2''' * '''Author:''' Brian "twigg" Terwilliger * '''Published:''' Dec 31, 2000
Well, the Gamers Guild in Clifton Park NY was named the Retailer of the year, as well as home of the 2000 World Champ, 2000 World Team Champs, and NY’s SW and YJ State Champs. With the help of my dad (biggest twigg - aka Marty) we got maad support, even reflections 2. Now, at the bottom of the TR will be some spoilers, so enjoy, but read the TR as well!!!! Decks: Light- EBO, Baraguains, and Missles... Dark- Hunt Down Surprise! Game 1 Light vs Todd Schnitzer’s Skum I set up EBO pretty fast, and he sets up his skum drains. The baraguians are retrieving machines and my missles are bouncing in and out of my lost pile. Meanwhile my b wings are holding space with barriers in hand... and he plays no ships. Mid late game I’m losing virtually no force and draining for 9 in space (@ yavin, hoth, and sullust). A late surprise assault did him in. FW +31 2 (+31) Good - baraguains working like a charm and him missing a critical hidden weapons! Bad - none Ugly - him not playing ANY space Game 2 Dark vs Jonny Chu’s X-Wing Swarm Well Hunt Down Surprise is the Twigg Hunt Down Odds deck - o - death. Undefeated and just a machine to handle. Only playing 9 charachters, my red selection is the best the dark side has to offer. Ok against Chu he ditched insights for honor, and I was very happy ;-). Vader, Empy and and Terk Mor destiny draw GAVE AWAY the odds. Jon looked at me and said CRAP! In space he is draining me and I set up my mega odds and insert. Meanwhile I’m draiing for 1 or 2, he’s canceling w/ rebel fleet. He activates, the odds never pops. So he retrieves with 6 wings on the table to get his insights back, (nice play!) So with a little luk, he gets insights on the table w/o an insert popping at all. Brian is very sad (especially when i could have dropped coward that turn and didn’t!!!!). So I set up my dueling destinies and I’m waiting for the mains, since visage is hurting him. The game is close by this point, each with like 15-20 life left. He drains me at 3 systems in space (still unflipped) and i loose 1 at corlag, 1 at kessel, and the counter assault his endor drain for 16 damage!!! A few turns later, Visage ends the game. FW +19 4 (+50) Good - Beating the best Xwing deck on the planet Bad - Odds NOT WORKING Ugly - Endor will never be the same... Game 3 Light vs Art Wright’s Hunt Down Duel Art had just beaten Chris, so I had to get revenge. (Last week Art beat Matt "The World" Sokol). But I had faith in my light. He sets up dockingbays and such and I get ebo out, V E R Y slowly... Im taking early Visage damage, termintate it once. He gets it back, senses my second trans, but I get him with the 3rd. ;-) Then Vader and Dengar and Mara w/ stik invade Hoth, and He’s looking to cancel my ebo. Fig Dan and Baraguians are keeping me in the game with lots of retrieval despite Secret Plans on the table. In space I get drains off and Battle Order is keeping him at bay. But then he gets janus to a db and gets around order. I never deployed Luke or Obi in fear of the duel. No dueling protection. Just big destinies. So I pay to drain, and start to hammer away at him in space w/ weapons and Huge destinies. Late game Boush kills Mara and Obi slaughters Janus to finish the game off. FW +23 6 (+73) Good - Beating an up and comming player and dammit i love those b wings. Bad - Paying for all my drains slowed me down. Not getting Ebo fast enough. Ugly - r e t r i e v a l . . . Game 4 Dark vs Dan Sokol’s Y4 Main’s Dan saw my game w/ chu and knew inserts were comming. So I figured he’d start insights. He didn’t. So I charged right fo the inserts, only popping once, but got him for 7. Visage ate away at us both and a timely placement of Battle PLan maid the visage damage big. Dan is returning to the game from a small haitus of having a life! and learned an important sw lesson all over again. DONT LOOSE OFF THE TOP. When Kessel flopped into his lost pile, we each knew the game shifted to my favor. Vader found his way to Obi and Dueled him out of the game. After counting about 4 ships that he lost, i fugured i’d be in the clear so I dropped caridia with zuck in mist hunter and then, the executor. Visgae ate away some more and in the end, the odds and duel made the difference. FW +8 8 (+81) Good - Dueling and winning... Dan is a good player. Bad - PLaying a tight game w/ a friend isn’t always ez... Ugly - Kessel off the top. Game 5 Light vs Mike Panayotou’s Big Blue Space I get ebo, VERY fast. Empy hits the db, and starships appear in space. We play cat n’ mouse a bit, while a bwing packin a missle drains for 2 at alderaan for the entire game, (woo-hoo!). The baraguians are making his drains do me no damage, and we chase each other around. I blow up the Devastator and a Dreadnaught (props to mike, we had a miscommunication and he was kool about me fixing the mistake. Pure sportsmanship... i hooked him up w/ a R1 pack...) In late game he drops EPP vader to the 4th marker to solidfy decree. Luckily Epp Obi, Luke and Boush were there to rid of the sith and make mike loose 10 force as well. A late shuffle at Alderaan and the death star put it away for my bwing deck of death!!!! FW +31 10 (+112) Good - Ebo fast is good. I also was able to beat a really good space deck! Bad - The miscommunication... Ugly - once again... r e t r i e v a l! So at this point the tourney is a lock, I win, woo-hoo!! And so I’m guaranteed some of the good stuff, and the tourney was going fine. But i realized I hadn’t played someone yet, and well, I was due... Game 6 vs Little Twigg’s Y4 Main’s Well let me start off by saying this game was horrible!!!! (chris is smiling over my shoulder as I type this!!!) He knew my tricks, he knew my secrets, and he knew my deck card for card. Well needless to say, no odds, no nothing. I tried the duling thing but Obi and Luke wussed out and sat at the Home One DB ALL GAME!!!. During the game the emperor got his @#$% kicked and the executor was dropped like a bad habit. Well hmm... REALLY not much to tell. We chased each other around and, I lost! FL -10 10 (+102) Good - NONE Bad - No odds, no dueling... Ugly - I LOST BECAUSE OF THE RULES!!! HOME ONE DB IS A GAY CARD. WHY CANT I MOVE THERE (terok mor and a pof occupied it do I could try and move vader over, but noooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo...) Here are the some of the top finishers out of 25 players... Twigg 10 +102 fooosheeezeee!!! Jon Chu 10 +75 Little Twigg 10 +64 Mike D’amboise 8 +45 Joe Giannetti 8 +24 Matt Sokol 8 +23 Dan Sokol 8 +22 Biggest Twigg 8 +21 Aaron Kingery 8 +12 What you want... SPOILERS!!! Luke Skywalker, Rebel Scout Rebel - Dest 1 - Deploy 7 - Forfeit 8 - Power 6 - Ability 6 - P/W/DSII icon - May cancel immunity to attrition of any vehicle here. If escorted by Vader and Take your father’s place on table, during your move phase may relocate Vader (with Luke) to Death Star II: Throne Room. Immune to Always thinking with your stomach and attrition < 5. Leebo Droid - Dest 3 - Deploy 2 - Forfeit 4 - Power 2 - Armor 4 - P - May be battled. While aboard any freighter, adds 2 to hyperspeed and may draw one battle destiny if not able to otherwise. If you have completed Rycar’s Run or Kessel Run, opponent loses 1 force (2 if both) during each of your control phases. Artoo & Threepio Droid - Dest 3 - Deploy 3 - Forfeit 6 - Power 2 - P/Ast- May pilot only falcon. All droids may be battled. Any player that has no ability in a battle takes no battle damage. Once per turn may take one card with "bad feeling" in title into hand from reserve deck; reshuffle. Bad feeling have I is suspended. ps - want these cards now? go to ebay and search "Star Wars CCG [card name]" I’m out... laaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaate!

Brian Terwilliger Twigg The NYC Reflecti.title: Brian Terwilliger Twigg The NYC Reflections 2 Sealed (tournament report)

main.content:
'''Brian Terwilliger Twigg The NYC Reflections 2 Sealed (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Brian Terwilliger]] posted on DeckTech on 13 February 2001 about [[February 2001 New York City Reflections II Booster Draft tournament]].[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-13-twigg-the-nyc-reflections-2-sealedd1728/ twigg-the-nyc-reflections-2-sealed], DeckTech (Brian "twigg" Terwilliger, 13 February 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-13-twigg-the-nyc-reflections-2-sealedd1728/ GitHub Pages]. Brian Terwilliger went 3–1, 6 (+32), with a Light Reflections II draft deck at the February 2001 New York City Reflections II booster draft, finishing about 4th; his only loss was to Marco Habert, who with Aaron Kingery took the expanded sheets. == Report info == * '''Author:''' [[Brian Terwilliger]] (byline: Brian "twigg" Terwilliger) * '''Published:''' 13 February 2001 (DeckTech) * '''Report title:''' ''Twigg The NYC Reflections 2 Sealed'' * '''Event:''' [[February 2001 New York City Reflections II Booster Draft tournament]] * '''Event date:''' 10 February 2001 * '''Site:''' Neutral Ground, New York City, New York * '''Finish:''' 4th ("or something") * '''Record:''' 3–1 * '''Points:''' 6 (+32) * '''Light deck:''' Reflections II draft deck (foil Kiffex, Independence, Crix Madine) == Games == Games as the author describes them; margins are as stated in the report. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Round !! Opponent !! Author's deck !! Opponent's deck !! Result !! Margin |- | 1 || NYC player with Japanese Vader || [[Light]] Light draft deck (Independence, Gold Leader) || Jabba's Palace deck with Gailid and Japanese Vader || Win (Terwilliger forgot his name) || +23 |- | 2 || [[Steve Baroni]] || [[Light]] Light draft deck (Independence, Gold Leader) || Jabba's Palace deck with foil Lord Vader and Emperor || Win || +7 |- | 3 || [[Marco Habert]] || [[Light]] Light draft deck (Independence, Gold Leader) || Jabba's Palace deck (Snoova with Vibro-Ax, Thrawn) || Loss || −9 |- | 4 || [[Michael Dalton]] || [[Light]] Light draft deck (Independence, Gold Leader) || Jabba's Palace deck with Imperial-class Star Destroyer and Limited Resources || Win (report spells him 'Michael Daulton') || +11 |} == Other results named in the report == * 1st (took a Reflections II expanded sheet): [[Marco Habert]] * 1st (took a Reflections II expanded sheet): [[Aaron Kingery]] == Original report == '''twigg-the-nyc-reflections-2-sealed''' * '''Author:''' Brian "twigg" Terwilliger * '''Published:''' Feb 13, 2001
OK, break time after the constructed consisted of this... microwaving a nasty chicken sandwhich, eating a Kit-Kat, and then getting battlegrounds for like 12 people. So Chris and I grab the binders and people start yelling, I need Mos Eisley, I need jundland wastes... it was a saad day for the binder that day, but all is well!!! Well around like 4:10 they start, (MEGA PROPS TO THE SEALED GUYS THIS TOURNEY WAS RUN DAM SMOOTHLY!!!) I get light side and I was hoping for dark, because the dark R2 expanded cards are WAY better than the light ones, but what are ya gonna do? So, my draft circle had me, Doug Faust, my dad, and 3 guys (sorry forgot ur names...) After all the drafting, here is what my deck looked like. Not great, but I was happy... Kiffex (foily!) Kessel (WHITE BOARDERED!!) Mos Eisley Death Star: Trash Compactor (mega tech!) Tat: Cantina Tat: Jundland Waste (sweet!) Cloud City: Carbon Chamber X wings x2 Y Wing Gold LEader in Gold 1 (pretty!!) Independance (foily!) B Wing Z95 Headhunter (wish i had a cloud!) Luke Skywalker, Rebel Scout Princess Leia Organa Crix Madine (shiny!) Rebel Trooper Elom Gran (the guy that retrieves a force when u battle at his site...) Cloud City Trooper Woikelette CZ3 R2X2 Rennek Beru Lars Owen & Beru Tibrin Operative Corillean Operative Rectenna (jap!!!) Proton Torpedo Subservo Swoop Spaceport Speeders Bith Shuffle Rebel Barrier Draw Their Fire It could be worse Escape Pod Nabrum Leidus and well, Steve B. pulled Foil Lord Vader and alpy, another guy pulled foil Jedi Luke, and another Pulled Jap Vader. So the hush of the crowd dies down and we started. Btw, I DIDNT PLAY MY BRO, (woo-hoo!!!) Game 1 vs NYC player w/ Jap Vader (sorry dude forgot your name...) He starts Jabba’s Palace and gets all the sites out, I start Kiffext, and drop an x wing there turn 2. He sets up GAILID and guys at the Audience Chamber and at the Palace. He then dropped a tie to his Tat system. I looked in my hand and saw the Independance. HUGE! So I’m sucking up drains on the ground and tracking my it could be worse. So the independance lands ontop of the TIE and he looses 6 force. I then send my guys, (how puny they REALLY are after his on the ground. Luke Rebel Scout join the chamber and a traked 5 clears it. Then the Jap vader cam down, but barrier stoped him, (whew!). My turn I dropped 2 droids and battled with that 5 again, killing vader. Meanwhile My darins at Kessel, Tat, and Kiffex were putting a major hurt on him. We squandered around and I eventually drain him out. FW +23 2 (+23) Good: Independance is .... big! Bad: Gailid and Vader is NASTY!!! Ugly: Poor lil’ tie... Meanwhile, Deck and my dad were going at it for the "Battle Of Marist" Read Mike Gemme’s sealed tr for more info... btw deck my dad awaits the second battle... Game 2 vs Steve Baroni’s Ultra Foily Deck He starts Jabba’s Palace, BIG surprise. I get a god draw, and drop a b-wing to kessel, the z95 to Kiffex and an operative to the Trash Compactor. He was flipping out, but he then dropped the shiny Lord Vader at the Junland and set up a palace drain. He is killing me on the ground and his BARGAINING TABLE was ruthless, totally taking the sting out of my drains. So I’m dealing him very little damage and his guys are starting to poressure me. Leia hits the Carbon Chamber, and is visited by ALOT of his imperials and aliens. Maybe hmmm 7-8. So Leai eats it and i loose 7. I then send operatives and dumb aliens and Luke into the chamber to smacsh on Palpy. Draw their fire is VERY cruital in this late game. I battle, he had 1 in hand and 1 in deck, limited resources leaves, and I win the battle, and the game, mainly because he didnt have an alien to canel my kessel drain that turn. FW +7 4 (+30) Good: A freaking AWESOME game w/ STEVE... Bad: Poor Leia... Ugly: Poor Leia... Game 3 vs Marco Habert Good ol’ Marco decides to show up and we hook him up with battle grounds. So he starts the..... Palace, yep thats right. So he draws , and draws and draws and draws and draws. I get NO SHIPS. NONE, ZERO, no ootang poo, NOTHING!!! So I get wrecked on the ground my Snoova w/ vibro, Judo w/ a blaster (he is nasty!!!) and Thrawn and a bunch of other guys. He then has 2 ties at my kiffex and shoots the b-wing i was able to get there. A lot of skirmishing and a good/tight game.. There is nothing really to report. He had power and weapons, alot of WEAPONS! And I never saw my ships. FL -9 4 +(21) Good: Playing Marco, thats really it... Bad: Getting slaughtered on the ground Ugly: His ENDLESS rant to Lingrell... ;-) Albany’s Aaron Northrup get’s paired with Marco for the title match. And a whole bunch of, if - then’s is the second match of Aaron KIngery and Chris Terwilliger. And at the 3rd table... Game 4 vs Michael Daulton He starts Palace... blah blah blah, ;--), I get ships early and I got Kessel turn 3 which was hot! So Im draining thinking everythig is kool. Then... an Imperial Class Star Destroyer, w/ Admiral Piet and Some 3/3 guy DESTROY’s my lone b wing. I losse a bajillion force (he only drew a 1 for destiny kinda helped!) and So i back up my kiffex drain and head to the ground. His Retwin is getting me back into the game b/c of draw their fire. I spread out my guys and use my destinies to fight back. I take the chamber w/ Luke and, then he limited resources me... AUUUGGGHHH! We all know that sux. So here I’m thinking its all over. But then he battled me or something, i drew a 6 clearing away his dudes at Tat : JP and My retaliation with like a rebel trooper and maybe and elom along with my drain of 4 did him in. FW +11 6 (+32) Good: A great game with Daulton! Bad: Limited gives me the chillz... Ugly: Poor Bwing, suked to be him, eh? Well Marco and Aaron Kingery were the top dudes taking home Reflection 2 Expanded Sheets, which there are only 5 sets of in Existamce! I got 4th or something, not bad. All in all this was a really great day. Part of the surprise was releaseing early versions of Qui-Gon and Darth Maul for the Ep1 Tat set... Maul is a 7/6 with built in dueling. (not an imperial or alien a MAUL icon...) and Gui-Gon is a 6/7 Jedi Master Icon who makes aliens power -1 at same site and is IMMUNE to attrition. Each of them had Episode 1 icons and something tells me there will be, "type II" events where only Episode 1 cards are allowed or even Objectives that only allow episode 1 cards. We’ll see... And now, part II of the Props and Slops: Props: Eric De’Luca for his story of leaving the Guild in hopes to get ass. Mike D’Amboise for comming up this weekend Slops: To the plattsburgh bus system for leaving w/o my boy matty sokol. Dont they KNOW WHO HE IS!!!! Cya kids... -twigg

'''Lore:''' Dark Lord of the Sith. Servant of the Emperor. Clad in armor containing a cybernetic life-support system. Was a pupil of Obi-Wan Kenobi. The best pilot in the galaxy and also a cunning warrior. '''Game text:''' During battle, you may add 1 to each battle destiny number (not 1 to the total, but 1 for each draw). A starship he pilots has power +3. If aboard Vader's Custom TIE, it has power +4 and maneuver +3. Immune to attrition < 5. '''Comparison with the English printing:''' The Japanese text explicitly explains that the bonus applies to each draw rather than the total; the English printed text says it adds 1 to each battle destiny. The Japanese uses 'pilot' where the English lore says 'starpilot.' The conditional wording also says he may add the bonus. |notes='''Darth Vader (Japanese Reflections II Foil)''' is a Japanese-language foil printing of [[Darth Vader]], released by [[Decipher]] as a case topper for [[Reflections II: Expanding the Galaxy]] in January 2001.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], p. 21. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive]. Its checklist rarity is P.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Star Wars Customizable Card Game Complete Card List v4.0], p. 30, Reflections II foil cards, R10. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009184033/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/swccgcardlist4.0.pdf Internet Archive]. Each case of six Reflections II booster boxes included one Japanese Darth Vader foil as a case topper. Each box also included one randomly selected foil box topper: [[Boba Fett With Blaster Rifle]], [[Han With Heavy Blaster Pistol]], [[Leia With Blaster Rifle]] or [[Obi-Wan With Lightsaber]].[https://store.starwarsccg.org/product/reflections-2-complete-foil-set-105-foils/ Reflections 2 Complete Foil Set], Star Wars CCG Players Committee Store. [[Dark Maneuvers]], everyone plays with them, or should. :) A basic necessity in those 'mediocre' decks which don't have 4 Star Destroyers. If you are relying upon your TIEs for space superiority, or at least defence, these cards are a necessity. These cards operate on two levels, offensively and defensively. There's the extra 1 power, which isn't that exciting, but in the case of underestimated or overestimated chances, it makes a difference of three force per card. If you have a hand of three of these babies, that's 9 force, not bad for a used interrupt. Defensively, well there's no way to MISS a tie scout with proton torpedoes unless you use this card. It's nice to be able to protect your ships in a time of need. (I know that's not in keeping with the Empire's philosophy of throwaway ships, but I never said the game was perfect) The fact that it's a 6 destiny and a USED interrupt are a big bonus in my mind, the more you use them, the more often they come up, the more damage you're doing. It's a great card as long as it's not in a deck with lots of low destiny required such as those with a lot of [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]]/Alters. Best Combo: Obviously, TALLON ROLL. A bonus of 4, for free. Plus an extra power in the ensuing battle after you've killed [[Pops]] in gold 5 with his r2, the proton torpedoes, and a rebel pilot. Just make sure to have enough [[Dark Maneuvers]]. The more the better! February 2001 New York City Reflections.title: February 2001 New York City Reflections II Booster Draft tournament

main.content:
'''February 2001 New York City Reflections II Booster Draft tournament''' was a Star Wars CCG booster draft held in Neutral Ground, New York City, New York on 10 February 2001. [[Aaron Kingery]] and [[Marco Habert]] won it. It is known from Mike Gemme's tournament report.<ref name="tr-d1726">[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-12-2-10-nyc-sealed-search-for-r2-sheetd1726/ 2-10-nyc-sealed-search-for-r2-sheet], DeckTech (michael "Deck" Gemme, 12 February 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-12-2-10-nyc-sealed-search-for-r2-sheetd1726/ GitHub Pages].</ref> It was played alongside the [[February 2001 New York City tournament]].

* '''Date:''' 10 February 2001
* '''Site:''' Neutral Ground, New York City, New York
* '''Format:''' [[Reflections II Booster Draft]]
* '''Winner:''' [[Aaron Kingery]] and [[Marco Habert]]

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive] (8 October 2026). |strategy=By Tom Lischkehttps://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/ghhhk.html Dark Side C2 [[A New Hope]] [[Ghhhk]] and its lightside counterpart, [[Houjix]], open up a whole new type of deck construction with the release of [[A New Hope]]. In the Premiere set, 'getting wide' to augment force drains was a dangerous proposition. Having only one or two characters or starships at each location invited an overwhelming counterattack, with a huge amount of battle damage typically resulting. Even if the player being attacked had an interrupt to cancel the battle, there was always the danger that the attacker had a [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]] to cancel the [[Hyper Escape]] or [[Narrow Escape]]. [[Ghhhk]] now allows the loser of the battle to eliminate all battle damage. It is immune to [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]], so the worst thing the LS player can do is hit it with What Are You Tryin To Push On Us or [[Grappling Hook]]. With eight to ten Ghhhks in a deck, the DS player can include many locations and cheap characters/starships to get a good force drain established before the LS can respond. When Obi, [[Luke Skywalker{{!}}Luke]], and [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]] (along with the [[Jedi Presence]] and Destiny Adders) show up to attack that [[Stormtrooper]] draining in the [[Tatooine: Cantina (Dark){{!}}Cantina]] with a Presence of the Force for 3 a turn, the DS can forfeit the [[Stormtrooper]] and play [[Ghhhk]] to eliminate the battle damage. For spice, she can play a [[Lone Warrior]] to force the LS to lose [[Han Solo{{!}}Han]]. The next turn, the DS can continue draining at the other 4 [[Tatooine (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Tatooine]] sites in play. If the LS player spreads thin to try to stop the drain, DS may respond by playing that [[Darth Vader{{!}}Vader]] or [[Kitik Keed'kak]] they have been holding. This strategy works extremely well in space also. The key is having enough locations and cheap deploys in the deck to maintain the force drain throughout the game. And most importantly, always have a [[Ghhhk]] in hand. Cards to watch out for: [[Grimtaash]]. The DS should stop drawing when there are two or three Ghhhks in hand, or run the risk of having the deck crippled by this card. [[Grappling Hook]]. If one of the Ghhhks gets grappled, the DS should make sure adequate forfeit is maintained at all sites to avoid a debilitating battle loss. Combos: [[Ghhhk]] + Stormtroopers (TIEs) (Jawas) + [[Lone Warrior]] ([[Lone Pilot]]) ([[Moment Of Triumph]]). One of the keys to the force drain deck is maintaining more characters or ships on the table. It helps to add some attrition to knock off a few of the LS characters or ships. [[Ghhhk]] + WED 15-17 'Septoid droid'. Adding a few of these attrition soaks can help protect some of the stronger characters in the deck. If the attack continues next turn, maybe [[Ghhhk]] will become necessary. These work well at sites where the DS has established 4 ability, and thus, a destiny draw. [[Ghhhk]] + [[Presence Of The Force]] + [[Organa's Ceremonial Necklace]]. These cards help the force drain. They fit better in a [[Ghhhk]] deck than a lightsaber because the 'saber has to be protected. The point of playing with [[Ghhhk]] is that the DS player does not mind losing any given character or ship. [[Ghhhk]] + [[Imperial Holotable]] + [[Monnok]] + [[Ng'ok]]. Just another site to force drain at. Just one [[Ghhhk]] can keep the LS player from draining there every turn as the DS can deploy on her turn, and withdraw during the LS deploy phase. [[Ghhhk]] + [[Mosep]]. [[Mosep]] should be one of the prime force drain members, as the loss will come straight from the LS reserve deck. [[Ghhhk]] + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Defel]]. [[Defel]] under night time conditions fits the theme of this deck perfectly, as he can avoid combat, thus saving the use of the [[Ghhhk]], and still be there for the counter attack. 8/21/96 These cards are extremely versatile and can almost always help add to your force drain or lessen your opponents. Here's how. If you're getting Force drained for 3 or more (the more the better) at any site, deploy a talz/stormtrooper/x-wing/tie or other similar low deploy card. You will then block the force drain on your opponents turn. He/she will then have to spend a Force to initiate (mabye more if he targets weapons, etc.). You merely lose the one card and the [[Houjix]]/[[Ghhhk]]. Thus, if he/she was going to Force drain for five you would instead lose only the [[Houjix]] and character. Another great use for these cards is the following. Pick a remote spot (a site with no adjacent areas) where you can Force drain for one or, if possible, two. If you have a spy, look for a 2/0 Force site (war room). Deploy a character there. Your opponent will be forced to deploy characters to block the Force drain and then battle you. When he/she does, lose your two cards. He/she has used up a good deal of Force killing your character and has now stranded (barring a Nabrun/Elis) one or more characters on this remote site. If it is a 2/0 site then he/she can't force drain either. These cards are also a must if you use undercover spies. If your opponent Alters your [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] effect, you will most likely be caught with just one card defending against a rather large group. Without the [[Houjix]]/Ghhk cards you could lose a good deal of Force. |combos=* [[Ghhhk]] + [[Imperial Holotable]] + [[Mosep]] [[Mosep]] should be one of the prime force drain members, as the loss will come straight from the Light Side Reserve Deck.Players Committee, [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab/Dark.json swccg-card-json Dark.json], Ghhhk (GEMP ID 2_132, commit d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab), attributes the two strategy recommendations to combinations with Imperial Holotable and Mosep, and with Sunsdown and Defel. These are strategy recommendations, not original printed text or a requirement that Mosep occupy a holosite. For the separate damage-cancellation ruling, see [https://web.archive.org/web/20260422134639/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf 2023 Advanced Rulebook], p. 144, Ghhhk: cards incapable of being forfeited are ignored. Decipher's [https://web.archive.org/web/20061215115652/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Glossary Version 2.0] (November 1998), p. 65, clarifies the original battle-damage function; its entry is not marked Errata, and p. 2 applies clarified gameplay to all versions. Preserved data copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020183206/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab/Dark.json Internet Archive] (20 October 2026). Lookup: [https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Ghhhk Scomp: Ghhhk]. * [[Ghhhk]] + [[Sunsdown]] + [[Defel]] [[Defel]] under 'night time conditions' fits the theme of this deck perfectly, as he can avoid combat, thus saving the use of the [[Ghhhk]], and still be there for the counter attack. |rulings=* Cards that cannot be forfeited (such as a character not participating in battle, or a [[Floating Refinery]]) do not prevent a player from canceling all remaining battle damage. |pulled_by=* [[Masterful Move]] * [[Masterful Move]] & [[Endor Occupation]] |cancels=* All remaining battle damage if you just forfeited all cards that participated in a battle you lost * [[Nightfall]] |characteristics=* dejarik |counterpart=* [[Houjix]] |has_refs=1 }}

Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive] (8 October 2026). |strategy=By Mike Watkins 8/21/96https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/light/small/houjix.html > These cards are extremely versatile and can almost always help add to your force drain or lessen your opponents. Here's how. If you're getting Force drained for 3 or more (the more the better) at any site, deploy a talz/stormtrooper/x-wing/tie or other similar low deploy card. You will then block the force drain on your opponents turn. He/she will then have to spend a Force to initiate (mabye more if he targets weapons, etc.). You merely lose the one card and the [[Houjix]]/[[Ghhhk]]. Thus, if he/she was going to Force drain for five you would instead lose only the [[Houjix]] and character. Another great use for these cards is the following. Pick a remote spot (a site with no adjacent areas) where you can Force drain for one or, if possible, two. If you have a spy, look for a 2/0 Force site (war room). Deploy a character there. Your opponent will be forced to deploy characters to block the Force drain and then battle you. When he/she does, lose your two cards. He/she has used up a good deal of Force killing your character and has now stranded (barring a Nabrun/Elis) one or more characters on this remote site. If it is a 2/0 site then he/she can't force drain either. These cards are also a must if you use undercover spies. If your opponent Alters your [[Undercover]] effect, you will most likely be caught with just one card defending against a rather large group. Without the [[Houjix]]/Ghhk cards you could lose a good deal of Force. |combos=* [[Houjix]] + [[BG-J38]] Adds 2 to the destiny of each of your holograms and dejariks drawn for battle destiny or weapon destiny.[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Houjix Scomp: Houjix]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). '''Decipher (Promotional Foil)''' — '''this page''' (8_126*) |sources=* [https://web.archive.org/web/20081225225012/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/index.html Star Wars CCG cardlists index] at Decipher.com (archive, 25 December 2008) * [https://web.archive.org/web/20070928014432/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/swallcards.pdf Complete Card List] (Decipher PDF, archive 28 September 2007) — Dark Effect: Imperial Arrest Order, Endor, U * Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2, pp. 34, 87.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 34, 87. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive] (8 October 2026). |strategy=By [mailto:jediknight@decipher.com Justin Pakes, Jedi Knight]https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/endor/dark/small/imperialarrestorder.html [[Imperial Arrest Order]] A great defensive card with some unique multiple functions to make up for that valuable card slot you have spent. For starters, you have an effect that can be started with using your trusty Twi'ilek Advisor. Secondly, you are putting a crimp in the mains and toys decks most no-brainer offensive weapon - [[Nabrun Leids]]. Restricting the sites and the timing of those transport actions means suddenly that Nabrun/Elis is a MOVEMENT card, not a force draining or beat down card. The [[Death Star]] never looked so safe! Now that's peace of mind. But if Light Side deploys enough to battle you anyway, add 2 to the forfeit of those Imperials who fall in the unique character midrange. And that's not all! To make up for the fact that your movement options are a little more limited, you can get a [[Cloud City: East Platform (Docking Bay){{!}}Docking Bay]] from Reserve once per turn. This can be a handy way to complete Utinni's (using generic Spaceport: Docking Bays) or even just a useful destiny tracking mechanism. It's a card that's hard to do without! Combo: = forfeit 7. = forfeit 7 ! And no battel damage or attrition if you have another Biker Scout there! |rulings=* Read this as owner's move phase and ''any'' exterior sites (not as owner's move phase and ''owner's'' exterior sites).[https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Imperial%20Arrest%20Order Scomp: Imperial Arrest Order]; card data [https://github.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/blob/d4e661ec/Light.json swccg-card-json Light.json] (commit d4e661ec). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive] (8 October 2026). |strategy=By James Kendrickhttps://web.archive.org/web/20020804005932/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/premiere/dark/small/imperialbarrier.html First of all, it's a destiny 4 used interrupt, making it pretty easy to recycle as your opponent will likely deploy characters or starships. This is also an annoying tactic. You could do it whether you truly need to stop him or not. The core advantages of this card is the pure surprise factor. Deploy a few characters to the Defensive Perimeter while keeping a [[Blizzard Walker]] and pilot in hand. When your opponent finally comes to get you, freeze him in his tracks with a Barrier. Then on your turn, deploy that walker and make him take some damage. The only problem with this card is that it's not immune to [[Sense (Dark) (Premiere){{!}}Sense]], and [[Skywalkers]] can cancel the Barrier as well. Try to have a [[Control]] or two when you rely on [[Imperial Barrier]] for protection. Combos: [[Imperial Barrier]] + [[I'd Just As Soon Kiss A Wookiee]] (my favorite). This is nasty in many ways. Delay an opponent, or use it to crush a lone character or starfighter that didn't plan on battling. As for your opponent's would-be [[Undercover]] spies, with [[Imperial Barrier]], they can't run or hide. Simply use the [[I'd Just As Soon Kiss A Wookiee]] on the [[Undercover]], and the [[Imperial Barrier]] on the spy. [[Imperial Barrier]] vs. opponent's deploying as a react. Joshua Grace Foil Japanese Vader Day Mir.title: Joshua Grace Foil Japanese Vader Day Mirkwood 2-6 (tournament report)

main.content:
'''Joshua Grace Foil Japanese Vader Day Mirkwood 2-6 (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Joshua Grace]] posted on DeckTech on 7 February 2001 about [[February 2001 Minneapolis tournament (6 February)]].[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-07-foil-japanese-vader-day-mirkwood-2-6d1710/ foil-japanese-vader-day-mirkwood-2-6], DeckTech (Joshua "Stormcrow" Grace, 7 February 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-07-foil-japanese-vader-day-mirkwood-2-6d1710/ GitHub Pages]. Joshua Grace finished 3rd at the Tuesday-night Mirkwood tournament in Minneapolis on 6 February 2001 with ISB Operations and a Throne Room mains deck, going 3–1 (6, +38) and losing only to Michael Raveling (playing Dion Erbes's decks) in the last round; Tim won the tournament and a foil Japanese Vader. == Report info == * '''Author:''' [[Joshua Grace]] (byline: Joshua "Stormcrow" Grace) * '''Published:''' 7 February 2001 (DeckTech) * '''Report title:''' ''Foil Japanese Vader Day Mirkwood 2-6'' * '''Event:''' [[February 2001 Minneapolis tournament (6 February)]] * '''Event date:''' 6 February 2001 * '''Site:''' Mirkwood, Minneapolis, Minnesota * '''Finish:''' 3rd * '''Record:''' 3–1 * '''Points:''' 6 (+38) * '''Light deck:''' Throne Room Mains deck with Ishi-Tech * '''Dark deck:''' [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB powerhouse w/DB's]] == Games == Games as the author describes them; margins are as stated in the report. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Round !! Opponent !! Author's deck !! Opponent's deck !! Result !! Margin |- | 1 || [[Rich Jeffery]] || [[Light]] Throne Room Mains with Ishi-Tech || [[Set Your Course For Alderaan / The Ultimate Power In The Universe|SYCFA Manipulator]] || Win (report: 'Rich Jeffries'; 2(+29)) || FW +29 |- | 2 || Nick || [[Dark]] [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB powerhouse w/DB's]] || [[Watch Your Step / This Place Can Be A Little Rough|(not-quite-Ravelling-style) WYS]] || Win (first name only (from St. Cloud); margin from running total 4(+42)) || FW +13 |- | 3 || [[Michael Raveling]] || [[Light]] Throne Room Mains with Ishi-Tech || [[Carbon Chamber Testing / My Favorite Decoration|Dion Erbes's CCT Hansicle]] || Win (report: 'Mike Ravelling', playing Dion Erbes's deck; margin from running total 6(+51)) || FW +9 |- | 4 || [[Michael Raveling]] || [[Dark]] [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB powerhouse w/DB's]] || [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Dion Erbes's Hidden Base (pure space)]] || Loss (rematch; 'whittling Mike's force down to a differential of 13'; final 6(+38)) || −13 |} == Other results named in the report == * 1st: Tim * 2nd: [[Michael Raveling]] * 4th: Nick == Original report == '''foil-japanese-vader-day-mirkwood-2-6''' * '''Author:''' Joshua "Stormcrow" Grace * '''Published:''' Feb 7, 2001
Usually, the Mirkwood tournaments draw 10 or a dozen players, but there are the occassional (and random) nights when a good-sized crowd will gather at Mirkwood for Star Wars CCG mirth and merriment. Tuesday’s tournament was one such tournament, gathering around 20 players, including Royce, a suprise guest from the Alderaan region who, much to my chagrin (and Scrye’s), opted not to play Rescue the Princess... Anyway, to continue the protracted preamble to this report, I went up to the register to fork over my dollar for the tournament (since I forgot to take one of my Cloud City packs from my apartment) and overheard Tim, the store’s co-manager, and Garrett, a player, talking about something when Garrett said, "We should really let Josh decide." Naturally, I asked, "Let Josh decide what?" Tim said that, due to my performance in Mirkwood tourneys over the past month, I had earned a foil Japanese Vader. The option (!) in this decision was that I could put it on the line, allowing the eventual tournament winner to claim the Vader. I actually thought about this for a few seconds; that’s my proof that I’m a sporting fellow. Then, like any sane individual, I took the Vader. And promptly traded him with Chad & Jerry for a Jedi Luke (yes, Chad & Jerry will get "props" this week instead of the usual trader "slops"). It turned out Tim had another foil Japanese Vader to throw on the line for the tournament winner, anyhow. So, feeling like less of a heel, I entered the tournament hoping to win a 2nd Vader. My chances were pretty good, I thought, since Mike Ravelling had decided to play Dion Erbes’ decks and let Dion play his. My Light Side was a Throne Room Mains deck with Ishi-Tech. Dark Side was an ISB powerhouse w/DB’s. Game 1: My Light Side vs. Rich Jeffries’ SYCFA Manipulator To make a short story shorter, we both dumped a bunch of sites out onto the table in the first couple of turns while I controlled the DS:DB early with Obi-wan. He put Vader down to battle Obi (and an Ishi-tib, I think), but a Fallen Portal was the end of Vader. Lucky draw, but that’s how it goes for me against Rich. No big surprise. So, then he put Mi’yoom at the Executor DB (?), planning to start his manipulation, and drew up... all of his cards! (??) So, Lando w/Axe, Luke w/Saber and some others came down to kill Mi’yoom with Draw Their Fire hitting the table, and shortly after Rich lost that battle, I ended the game with no lost pile. FW 2(+29) This has apparently put me in the top pairing which, with a foil Japanese Vader on the line, was pretty darn cool. Game 2: My DS against Nick’s (not-quite-Ravelling-style) WYS Having lost to Mike Ravelling’s broken WYS deck on Saturday, I decided to play cautiously, setting my forces up to avoid a multiple-destiny beat-down. This allowed Nick to get in a couple of early drains against me, but soon I had an undercover spy blocking his Cantina drain, Walkers and/or the Emperor (and the ominous Force Lightning) blocking all the battleground DB’s, and big blue in space at both Tatooine and Kessel (with enough destiny draws to crack his Falcon’s immunity). There wasn’t any battling since he played a barrier when I set Grand Admiral Thrawn and the Chimaera up against a lone Captain Han, and, from that point on, Nick was afraid to challenge my forces, and it just didn’t pay for me to attack him, since all his drains were cancelled each turn (or I would lose an ISB agent and retrieve him with the objective each of my turns). However, Nick made me pay for my impatience when I grabbed his Rebel Barrier. He must have played On the Edge 10 times and retrieved 4 force with it each time. Yet, the ISB lock- down proved too effective for him to overcome, and it was merely a matter of time before my drains overtook his retrieval. FW 4(+42) After this game, I managed to trade with Royce for a Smoke & Mirrors 5. X-Files may not be a popular game anymore, but it’s cheap, baby, and fun! I think I traded a Mon Cal cruiser for the X-Files equivalent of a Mara Jade (and her saber). Surprised to learn that Dion Erbes had an extensive X-Files collection, I taught him the rules for the advanced game. So, going into game 3, I was again in the top pairing, this time against my own personal Lex Luther (or am I his?), Mike Ravelling. But Mike was playing Dion’s decks, so I didn’t expect as tough a game as usual. (Meanwhile, Mike’s decks were 1-1.) Game 3: My LS vs. Mike Ravelling playing Dion’s CCT Hansicle I didn’t draw any 2/0 locations in my opening hand. Just the Home 1 DB. So I threw that down and searched for the Echo DB. Oola went out to the Home 1 DB for early generation and, hopefully, to get out an early lock. But Mike played his 1st turn intelligently (duh) drawing a handsize just above my activation and saved the rest of his force. On my 2nd turn, then, I deployed Leia w/Blaster to the Carbon Chamber and moved her over to rescue Han. With no Rebel Barrier in hand, I saved a force hoping to bluff Mike. But it was to no avail. Mike, in fact, had drawn a Mara and deployed her against Oola, fetched her saber and put First Strike on the table. Oola died, but Mara drew Mara for destiny, so the loss was recoverable. I hoped to take advantage of First Strike by throwing out Chewie Protector, KFC, some other scrub and Luke w/Saber against Mara. But Mike had the barrier for Luke. I don’t think I battled that turn. The next couple of turns saw me losing battles at the Home 1 DB while Mike was retrieving from First Strike. I eventually decided that it wasn’t worth the fight and had Luke transit the heck away. So it became a drain race for a while, and I was losing. But Mike attacked Leia and Cap’n Han with Ephont Mon and Mighty Jabba. When the smoke cleared, Ephont Mon had died along with Cap’n Han, but Mighty Jabba couldn’t afford to run his lard @$$ away from Leia before we all discovered that Han hadn’t died but had just run away to fetch his blaster. So I initiated battle, hit Jabba with Han, targetted again with Leia to add 5 from Aim High, and drew a total destiny of 9. Mike ended up losing Jabba and 11 force while Han took Advantage of the situation to run over to join Obi-wan and Major Hashish at the CC DB. I ate another drain of 2 at the Home 1 DB before I was able to deploy Boussh to block that site. Mike was now losing the drain race and attempted to retrieve force by battling Luke w/Saber and an Ishi-tib with Bane Malar. However, that move backfired when Luke sliced Bane and drew a 4 for destiny to Mike’s... 0 (I didn’t even have to lose the Ishi-tib). That pretty much summed it up. One or two more turns of draining ended the game. FW 6(+51) And it’s looking good so far since there are only 3 undefeated players left, and one of them, Tim, has a timed win. I’m 19 differential ahead of 2nd place and think I might get two Japanese foil Vaders in one night. Game 4: My ISB vs Mike Ravelling playing Dion’s Hidden Base Well, this wasn’t what I wanted. After the last game, I had breathed a sigh of relief and shook Mike’s sweaty hand... Only, as it turns out, to play Mike again. Royce, the other undefeated player with full wins, is on the same side as me, working his Alderaan tech with Scum. (Tim, meanwhile, is playing Light Side and *should* be playing me, but Decipher’s software doesn’t see things that way. And none of us realize this until after the game.) So Mike and I sit across from each other once again. I decide to start You Cannot Hide Forever in order to ditch it later for Search & Destroy. Mike starts Squassin, Wise Advice/Do or Do Not, and the effect that lets you forfeit weapons. So I think it’s a B-wing deck or such and joke that I’m not going to be stupid enough to deploy to space. I get an Emperor in my hand and deploy him for free to the Coruscant site, use IAO to get the Coruscant DB and move Palpy over. Along with Rendili, this gives me beaucoup activation early. Mike reveals Tycho to fetch Green Squadron 3 and set him up at Rendili. Well, I swallow my earlier comment about not deploying to space since my hand holds: the Executor, Chimaera, Grand Admiral Thrawn and that crazy Victory Class whose name I shall never remember. So I save force for a turn and deploy Thrawn in the Chimaera to his Barrier. Blah. We then battle frequently in space, and I lose. I can’t get agents on the ground to flip. I can’t set up Imperial Decree or Search & Destroy. I can’t kill Corran Horn. And, when on my 2nd turn I search for a docking bay, the only one in my deck is the <> DB that I want to deploy to Kessel, Kiffex or Coruscant. Except I forget that people who are playing pure space play the Coruscant system, so I deploy my generic docking bay to some drain-1 system instead. While I go about losing all my ships in battle (including Bossk which I draw later), I probe all of Mike’s systems except the correct one. In the end, I’m upset that I’m going to lose the foil Vader, but given my poor play, whittling Mike’s force down to a differential of 13 was an accomplishment. So, I go 6(+38). Royce loses his game by 4 or so. But Tim notches a 4th win to take the tournament and a foil Japanese Vader. Mike Ravelling gets 2nd. I get 3rd. Nick, who travelled down from St. Cloud for the tournament, defeats Royce, knocking him out of the top 4, to claim 4th for himself. Chad, Jerry, Justin Alfs and I discuss the possibility of taking what I know of the incredible, edible Middle Earth: the Drinking Game and modifying the rules for Star Wars CCG. Cheers: Tim for the big win! Mirkwood for all the tournaments and the great support. Chad & Jerry. To get them off my back. Graham for the surprise Cherry Coke. Mike Ravelling for being one of the few players to consistently play well enough to merit shaking a consistently sweaty palm. Jedi Luke being for destiny 6 (even if I never drew him). Foil Japanese Vader for being trade-bait for a Jedi Luke. Rich Jeffries, thanks for the auto-wins ;-P Royce, Nick, Nick’s brother, Sam, and Sam’s friend (even though he cheated) for joining in the fun. Royce for the Smoke & Mirrors 5. Jeers: Herb. Had to constantly avoid him. Decipher’s software. I get screwed weekly. Ex-girlfriends in general. Joshua "Stormcrow" Grace

The benefits of this card far outweigh using [[Control]] to cancel Force drains. Firstly, it is used and not lost. This is most important. At the end of the game you want to have as many cards left as you possibly can. Secondly, it has a destiny value of 4 while [[Control]] has a destiny of only 2. If you play with 4 or 5 in your deck, you will find them popping up very often allowing for very nice destiny draws. Mike Gemme 2-10 NYC The Search For Foile.title: Mike Gemme 2-10 NYC The Search For Foiled Sheets (tournament report)

main.content:
'''Mike Gemme 2-10 NYC The Search For Foiled Sheets (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Mike Gemme]] posted on DeckTech on 12 February 2001 about [[February 2001 New York City tournament]].[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-12-2-10-nyc-the-search-for-foiled-sheetsd1717/ 2-10-nyc-the-search-for-foiled-sheets], DeckTech (michael "Deck" Gemme, 12 February 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-02-12-2-10-nyc-the-search-for-foiled-sheetsd1717/ GitHub Pages]. Mike Gemme went 2–2 at the February 2001 New York City tournament (Decipher Day at Neutral Ground) with a non-dueling Hunt Down deck and AITC Mains built by Hayes Hunter, beating Mike Dalton and Jason Robinette and losing to Dalton and Chris Praskac. == Report info == * '''Author:''' [[Mike Gemme]] (byline: michael "Deck" Gemme) * '''Published:''' 12 February 2001 (DeckTech) * '''Report title:''' ''2-10 NYC The Search For Foiled Sheets'' * '''Event:''' [[February 2001 New York City tournament]] * '''Event date:''' 10 February 2001 * '''Site:''' Neutral Ground, New York City, New York * '''Record:''' 2–2 * '''Points:''' 4 (+40) * '''Dark deck:''' [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Non Dueling Hunt Down (built by Hayes Hunter)]] * '''Light deck:''' [[Agents In The Court / No Love For The Empire|AITC Mains (built by Hayes Hunter)]] == Games == Games as the author describes them; margins are as stated in the report. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Round !! Opponent !! Author's deck !! Opponent's deck !! Result !! Margin |- | 1 || [[Michael Dalton]] || [[Dark]] [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|HDADTJ (non-dueling Hunt Down)]] || EBO Monkey X-wings || Win (Dalton rated 1979) || +6 |- | 2 || [[Michael Dalton]] || [[Light]] [[Agents In The Court / No Love For The Empire|AITC Mains]] || [[My Kind Of Scum / Fearless And Inventive|MKOS Abyssans]] || Loss (second game against Dalton) || −8 |- | 3 || [[Jason Robinette]] || [[Dark]] [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|HDADTJ (non-dueling Hunt Down)]] || Sullust deck? || Win (report spells him 'Jason Roubinette{sp?}' (1616); opponent conceded after a dispute over table layout) || +29 |- | 4 || Chris Packsac(?) || [[Light]] [[Agents In The Court / No Love For The Empire|AITC Mains]] || [[My Kind Of Scum / Fearless And Inventive|MKOS Skrilling]] || Loss (report gives 'Chris Packsac?' (2059)) || −23 |} == Other results named in the report == * 1st: [[Brian Terwilliger]] * 3rd: [[Steve Baroni]] == Original report == '''2-10-nyc-the-search-for-foiled-sheets''' * '''Author:''' michael "Deck" Gemme * '''Published:''' Feb 12, 2001
Prelude

This tourney was on very short notice, and me not having a car at college presented to be a giant problem for attending this event. I knew I could get a ride with the Albany guys, as I did last year for this same event. My girlfriend went home this weekend so I was strapped for a ride out to the Modena rest-stop to meet them. Luckily the little Indian girl that lives below me let me take her 2000 legacy and leave it on the side of the highway for 15 hours.

Event Horizon

After about an hour of sleep because this drunk girl stumbled into my apartment at 2am (right after I had gone to bed) and kept me up with my roommate until about 5, I wake at 6am shower, dawn my clothes for the day, pick up my bag and search for this girls car. I listen to the Gladiator soundtrack on the way there, and then I wait an hour for Albany to show up. The ride down is pretty uneventful as I just try and complete the decks that Hayes Hunter made for me at 12am the previous night. My decks for this are Non Dueling Hunt Down, and AITC Mains. He said I’d go four and O. My rating going into this is 1627 with 34 games. This is without Day 1 of worlds where I beat some 18 and 1900+ players, but also a 1-5 performance where I scrubbed out in Framingham. Away we go.

Game One – HDADTJ vs. Mike Dalton (1979) EBO Monkey Xwings

I call this monkey Xwings because he puts one at a system and hyper escapes when you engage him. He sets out slow and I get Mara with her saber at a docking bay to start draining because I know it is going to be a slow game. I got Choke Vader to the North Ridge because Commander Luke was their draining me and it pissed me off, so I Chocked him with an untracked 7. After that Vader must’ve just drained there although I for the life of me cannot remember what went on. But once he gets EBO going he puts these Xwings in space and starts draining heavy. He also gets Orders me to Engage, so I do and he hyper escapes so I still lose the three force. This and the drains in space kind of kill me, but on the other side I’ve been hitting him with Search and Destroy since turn three and Visage since turn one. I only lost to visage once this whole game. The lack of detail in this game of the report is because the deck lacked action itself. Either way I win, which is huge for me cause I am known as a scrub all across the land. FW by 6 (+6)

Highs: Beating Mike Dalton
Lows : Only winning by six, but I cant get greedy cause this deck kicked some ass

Game Two – AITC Mains vs. Mike Dalton (1979) MKOS Abyssans.

So I’m not too thrilled about playing Dalton again because he is a good player, probably better than me. Anyways, we start out, both on Tatooine, and get guys down. I put Obi at the Desert Heart to drain and he puts his Sail Barge with an abyssan and mercenary pilot on it and gets the passenger deck out. But he doesn’t put anyone on the passenger deck so I beat the thing down with Luke and some other people. He’s got Bib, Jabba and Boelo and the chamber doing some damage, which I can take. I get Harc Seff down with Luke again at the entrance cavern so I’m draining and covering his drains until Seff caught a beat down with Han later in the game. Xizor is deep into the palace on the other side of the Chamber so I get her down with Dash but he none shall passes dash, I battle they stay, he battles they stay. So I sorry about the mess the bastard and take him out. Then I’m draining him there for the rest of that game. Back to the Desert Heart with obi. Mad battles going on there all game, but I’ve been saving my Run Luke runs because Luke is having a good time draining at the Hutt trade route and I don’t realize I can react to my own battles, so pretty much the last battle of the game… I forget to use the run Luke run. Luke’s 6 power would have saved me the game. Instead I lose by 8. I’m pissed. FL by 8. 2(-2)

Highs: Doing what this Deck was supposed to do… I Guess.
Lows : Saving the Run Luke Run’s and forgetting to use them. I’m a bastard.

Game Three – HDADTJ vs. Jason Roubinette{sp?} (1616) Sullust Deck?

This guy starts Sullust and two effects with Heading to the medical frigate. Squad @#$% and the one that lets you forfeit weapons.

He gets out a mad space crew at sullust and I put Zuckuss with 4lom at carida. I also have Mara and a saber at the downtown plaza and Vader and his saber at the CC Docking bay. I am draining him like crazy and pinging him with S&D and Visage, which I only lose to once. He lost good things off the top like Wedge’s ship and stuff like that. Then deploys a Nebulon B frigate to Carida and tries to move the Outrider there and I’m like “you cant do that without leebo, you just can’t make it” and the guy explodes. “WHY ARE THE SITES SET UP LIKE THIS? CARIDA SHOULD BE ON THE OTHER SIDE!” Here is what it was, Sites on one side on the table, systems on the left. The order of sites went like this so I he says it should be between cloud city site and the Dstar site. And I’m like I just put it next to the system cause it makes sense to me like that. He yells at me some more and puts his hand out. I win by 29. I go and tell the Albany guys about it and they are sympathetic, but I feel bad, not only because the guy is a prick, but because I don’t want to win like that. Me and twigg and baroni all turn around and there he is bantering about the game to his boyfriend.. it was pretty sad. FW by 29 4(+27)

Highs: Winning by 29.
Lows : Doing it against a Schmuck.

Game Four – AITC Mains vs Chris Packsac? (2059) MKOS Skrilling

This game sucked. He pretty much beat me down Hard core. I kept putting up fights, but it was to no avail. I can’t remember much detail about this game as he just continued to smack me around left and right. I made some good moves like getting corran horn to the passenger deck to drain, but it was too late. I only got luke out once and it was when I had 9 cards left so I was able to get him down and battle. By then it was too late because he was retrieving all of the time and skrillings are just really strong in my opinion. Again, not a lot of details because there were none, just a lot of smacking down of obi, leia, and han. I couldn’t get Lando out with his vibrator either. So I lose by 23. FL by 23, 4 (+40)

Highs: None
Lows : Losing by a lot, not getting Luke out.

So there is the tourney, for prizes I win a Masterful Move foil instead of getting packs, which sucks cause I thought I would get the packs also. Brian Twigg won, my boy steve Baroni came in third which is great for a Kashyyyk player to go in and represent all over another region. All in all it was a good time, I really don’t want to write about the sealed deck because it just wasn’t that fun aside from me pulling a jedi Luke and having to give it up, and steve getting an Emporer and Lord vader foil passed to him… and he didn’t even win.

Hayes Hunter for giving me my dark deck
Me for beating mike Dalton
Art for giving me the ride and being a great TD
Aaron for being the funniest bastard of them all

Baroni for coming in third and being my boy

All of the Albany guys (deluca, walter, Erwin, etc etc) for hooking me up with rides and being good guys all together

Chris and Brian twigg for yelling “DECK” at all the right times
Scott Lingrel for running the sealed well and being the only one to say my last name correctly, also for being a good guy and introducing himself.

SLOPS

Me for losing to Mike Dalton
Art’s Feet for stankin on the way home
Aaron Kingery for letting his car get locked up overnight
Pete S for stealing all of my cards

I have nothing bad to say about the jet pack tech
I really have nothing bad to say about Northrup either

Erwin for being a bastard about getting back the Luke I borrowed, and it wasn’t even his.
Mr Twigg for blocking my drains with unpiloted red 1 (doh!)
Chris twigg for making fun of my (hayes’) decks
Brian twigg for losing a fight to me and aaron

'''Decipher (Promotional Foil)''' — '''this page''' (2_135o*) |sources=* [[Media:Decipher_Glossary_1998.pdf|Decipher Glossary Version 2.0]] (November 1998) * Original printed face: [https://web.archive.org/web/20080512231004/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/monnok.html Monnok], [[Decipher]] (archived 12 May 2008). * Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2, pp. 34, 87.[https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf SWCCG Collecting Encyclopedia 3.2], pp. 34, 87. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192828/https://res.starwarsccg.org/Resources/Star_Wars_CCG_Collecting_Encyclopedia_3.2.pdf Internet Archive] (8 October 2026). |strategy=By Gregg Keefer, Gold 4https://web.archive.org/web/20040811123219/http://www.decipher.com/starwars/cardlists/anewhope/dark/small/monnok.html 8/29/97 This little Dark Side Dejarik interrupt can ruin your opponent's day. In addition to being of use on a Hologame Board as a Dejarik creature with a destiny, power, ability, forfeit of 2, this card has two card stripping functions (one used and one lost) that can really disrupt a Light Side strategy. The used function is as follows: If opponent has 13 or more cards in hand place all but 8 (random selection) in Used pile. If your opponent hasn't got [[Traffic Control]] out they might have to draw several turns trying to get a certain card they need to nail you with. If he is digging and digging for that Asteroid Sanctuary or [[Echo Base Operations]] with a big fat hand and he suddenly smiles and stops drawing cards, that would be a good time to play a used [[Monnok]] on them! Watch their triumph become tragedy as the Dark Side dismantles the lovely fleet the rebels had assembled to attack the [[Death Star]]. This can have a beneficial effect for the Light Side player as well, since you are re-circulating Force for them, but in most cases this is offset by the damage it does to them strategically. Making them wait to assemble again while you perform normal operations to secure your Force drains will give you a foothold in new systems. The lost function is as follows: Use 4 Force to cause opponent to revel hand. All cards opponent has two or more of are lost. This can be a devastating hit if the light side is holding a lot of cards even in a carefully constructed deck. The four Force cost to play this lost function makes this a costly interrupt to attempt but it can pay off in spades if you combine it with a [[Scanning Crew]]! Pay one Force for the [[Scanning Crew]] to take a look at his hand and if you see some doubles you'll know whether you want to play the [[Monnok]] or not. Played at the right time this card can deliver a lot of damage in lost cards but the more painful loss to your opponent will be the limiting of his options in accordance with his intended strategy. Usually the cards that are multiples in a deck are the cards that the player is wanting to have access to quickly or often. If this option is removed along with the units of force you are well on the way to victory for the Empire. 8/21/96 Many of my friends play where they pick up millions of cards, then [[Traffic Control]] them back to their Used pile. Well, here's one way to stop it! Play [[Monnok]] during your turn, at the beginning of your control phase. You'd want to play [[Monnok]] as a USED interrupt, leaving them with only 8 cards in their hand. Again, this works best against players who hoard their cards. Anyways, with many cards back in their Used pile, play [[Trinto Duaba]] during your battle phase. With a good destiny draw, you might be able to take out a huge chunk out of their deck. The only thing you really have to watch out for are Senses, so stock Senses and Alters to counter them. There'll be Hell to Pay and [[Tentacle]] works well against them, too. |combos=* [[Monnok]] + [[Trinto Duaba]]Players Committee, [https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab/Dark.json swccg-card-json Dark.json], Monnok (GEMP ID 2_135, commit d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab): the named combinations with Trinto Duaba and Scanning Crew, and the Used-function hand-size initiation ruling. The original Used function places cards in the Used Pile for Trinto Duaba; Scanning Crew reveals hand information and can place a Rebel in the Used Pile. Decipher, [https://web.archive.org/web/20061215115652/http://decipher.com:80/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Glossary Version 2.0] (November 1998), p. 67, Grimtaash, explains the same 13-card initiation condition: responses reducing hand size do not stop the result. Preserved data copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261020183206/https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swccgpc/swccg-card-json/d4e661ec735dcb111266fbda98704f2181e1cfab/Dark.json Internet Archive] (20 October 2026). Lookup: [https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Monnok Scomp: Monnok]. * [[Monnok]] + [[Scanning Crew]] |rulings=* The Used function still has its result even if the opponent plays any response(s) that reduces their hand size below 13 cards. |pulled_by=* [[Masterful Move]] * [[Masterful Move]] & [[Endor Occupation]] |characteristics=* dejarik |counterpart=* [[Grimtaash]] |has_refs=1 |notes=* Decipher Glossary Version 2.0 Errata. Side-by-side faces: [[Errata]]. |see_also=* [[Errata]] * [[Monnok]] }}

'''Patrick Napier Colorado Springs A Shot At Foils 9-16-01 (tournament report)''' is the tournament report [[Patrick Napier]] posted on DeckTech on 17 September 2001 about [[September 2001 Colorado Springs tournament]].[https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/2001-09-17-colorado-springs-a-shot-at-foils-9-16-01d2976/ colorado-springs-a-shot-at-foils-9-16-01], DeckTech (Patrick "Pappy" Napier, 17 September 2001). Preservation copy: [https://stevetotheizz0.github.io/decktech_archives/reports/2001-09-17-colorado-springs-a-shot-at-foils-9-16-01d2976/ GitHub Pages]. Patrick Napier finished 2nd of 8 at an Episode I (Type II) tournament at Hobby Town, Colorado Springs, on 16 September 2001 with Senate decks on both sides, going 3–1 and losing only to the undefeated winner Thomas Harris. == Report info == * '''Author:''' [[Patrick Napier]] (byline: Patrick "Pappy" Napier) * '''Published:''' 17 September 2001 (DeckTech) * '''Report title:''' ''Colorado Springs A Shot At Foils 9-16-01'' * '''Event:''' [[September 2001 Colorado Springs tournament]] * '''Event date:''' 16 September 2001 * '''Site:''' Hobby Town, Colorado Springs, Colorado * '''Players:''' 8 * '''Finish:''' 2nd * '''Record:''' 3–1 * '''Points:''' 6 (+18) * '''Dark deck:''' [[My Lord, Is That Legal? / I Will Make It Legal|Senate Maul (a version of Dredlox Senate)]] * '''Light deck:''' [[Plead My Case To The Senate / Sanity And Compassion|Senators and Jedi (Senate with the Jedi Council Chamber, Radiant VII and Captain Madakor)]] == Games == Games as the author describes them; margins are as stated in the report. {| class="wikitable" |- ! I was not really sure I wanted to play any Episode I events, because the environment right now is fairly limited, and the Senate objectives seem like the only way to go. But then I saw the foil Darth Maul and Qui-Gon that are being sent out for prize support for these events and I quickly changed mind. Saturday before the event I started building decks at about 12:30 at night. Not too smart, I know. I decided to play a version of Dredlox Senate for the Dark Side, because it was already built and it would save me some time I needed for precious sleep. For Light Side I decided Senate was also the way to go, with the Jedi Council Chamber and a load of Jedi for ground control. I tossed in Radiant VII and Captain Madakor to handle any space. By 4:30 am, I had my decks made and I was ready to go to bed. The next morning I arrived at Hobby Town, and there were only a few players waiting for the store to open. I was hoping we would at least be sanctioned. While we were waiting for the store to open, we discussed the Episode I environment, and everyone agreed that the Dark Side had a definite advantage, and that the only reason most of us were there was for a shot at the foils. By the time Hobby Town opened its doors, we had eight players with TD Brian Montez included, and we were ready to play some Star Wars. NOTE : I will not be posting ratings in this report like I usually do, because most of the players in this event do not yet have an Episode I format rating. GAME ONE Senate Maul vs. Danny Hummel Hyperdrive Podracing Hmmm, a Hyperdrive deck in a Type II event ? I kind of figured that Senate would be the only way to go, but I could be wrong. ( By now most people know I am wrong more often than I should be ) Danny plays Nekkid Threepio and tries to set up some sort of Pile, but he only used Threepio once or twice. I set up a Senate majority one the first turn, and the Dark Side controlled the Senate for the rest of the game. Maul came out to play rather early as well, and with the Phantom Menace on the table, he is unstoppable. Danny makes me stack a few cards on Credits, but my senators are blocking the drains like mad. Danny wins the race after a few turns, because Sebulba STILL cannot drive a podracer to save his life, but Squabbling Delegates gets all the Force lost right back. By this time Danny has spread out all over Tatooine to drain away at me, but P-59 and P-60 make surgical strikes to limit Force loss. At the end of the game, Danny has one Force left. Instead of drajning him at the Senate, I decide it would be cool to take him out in style, and Maul confronts Qui-Gon for a final battle. I use Lott Dod to try to pull out a Maul Strikes, and its then I realize that in my deck building frenzy, I neglected to put one of those crucial cards in this deck that revolves around the Sith Apprentice. Great ! Danny loses Qui-Gon with no overflow, and survives to drain at me for one more turn. Note to self, when the game is yours, just end it, no matter how boring that end is. Full win by 8. So in the quest for the foil coolness, I start off at 2 ( + 8 ), so I need to win the next game by a huge differential. GAME TWO Senators and Jedi vs. Mike Minillo Podless Senators Mike said at the beginning of this game that he does not have a whole lot of Tatooine or Coruscant cards, so he thinks he cannot win. I guess he is here for the same reason we all are, for a shot at the foils. Mike deploys a couple guys to the Senate, and I let him have it for a turn or two. I have Plea To The Court in my opening hand to block that drain, anyway. Yoda sets up shop at the Council. On the third turn, I call the Light Senators to session, deploying Queen Amidala RON, Palpatine, Mas Amedda and Horox Ryyder. The battle clears out the Dark Side senators, and from that point on, the Senate was under Light Side control. In a senate majority Palpatine is a beast, and he rellay helps the battles going on elsewhere in the galaxy. Mike starts putting his Senators all over Tatooine, trying to drain, but the Jedi will have none of that. Qui-Gon makes short work of a couple Senators at Mos Espa. The rest of the game is pretty uneventful, as the Jedi take over Tatooine and the Senators keep doing their work. I recycle as many cards as I can and draw up my Might Of The republic to pull of some retrieval. In the end, Mikes lack of good cards cost him the game. Full win by ( + 25 ) That was a much better game, but unfortunately it was honestly against a relatively weak deck, so I knew I still had a long road ahead of me to get a shot at one of those foils. At this point, I am in first place overall, but as anyone who knows me can already guess, that was about to change. GAME THREE Senators and Jedi vs. Thomas Harris Podless Senators Thomas has really come up as a player, and is so far undefeated as well, but with a lower differential than me. We are the only players who have not lost at this point. Normally, I have no problem beating Thomas, but I had heard that his deck boasted FOUR The Phantom Menaces and just as many Mauls. At least he was not racing, which is a huge surprise to me, because Thomas usually does race in constructed environment tournaments. On his first turn, Thomas deploys two Senators and flips. I go through my deck for Yoda to deploy at the Council, but I come up short. Thomas then plays Podracer Collision used and places one of my Are You Brain Deads out of play. Great move, Thomas. After a few turns, I have Yoda, Depa Billaba, and Plo Kloon in the Council, and Maul has yet to make an appearance. The Senate is overrun by greedy shifty Dark Side Senators, so I set up my Political Effects to use to help out the Jedi in the upcoming battles. It was then that Thomas deployed the Young Apprentice to the Senate, said whazzup to Lott Dod, and strolled right into the Council Chamber. It took two battles to clear it out, and for the rest of the game, Maul was Force draining for four, laughing aat the fact that he had taken over that bastion of the Jedi. Qui-Gon invades Tatooine, as does a whole lot of my Senators, backed up by Panaka and his Gat. Rune Haako and some Destroyer Droids took notice and came to start some fights. Then, Thomas retrieves his entire Lost Pile with Squabble, Maul Alters Plea To The Court, and the drain race from that point is a losing battle. Full loss by 20. That game put a huge dent in my differential, putting me at 4 ( + 13 ) and those foils seemed like they were out of reach. The last game was going to make or break me. GAME FOUR Senate Maul vs. Josh Gilliom Hyperdrive Podracing Great, another game with podracing. Not to worry though, because this deck is designed to retrieve a decent amount of Force. I have added Sebulbas Podracer to the deck, just to help out against Podracing decks. Josh is a part of the Pueblo Crew, and they are not having the greatest day so far. This one as to go my way. I flash Anakin right away, and draw a 6. Its about time Sebulba figured out how to drive. I flip my objective on the second turn, and Lott Dod is having a good ole time rooting through my Force Pile every turn. Maul comes out to play against Obi-Wan, but he has not yet reached the rank of Jedi Knight, and when the smoke clears, Josh had drawn a 5 for battle destiny, killing the Sith to attrition. A few turns into the game, I Squabble to retrieve some of my Lost Pile, and the race is tied at 22. To Joshs dismay, I flash Anakin again and draw a 4, sealing the victory at the Boonta Eve Classic. I retrieve 6, and Josh loses 6, the usual. I look at Sebulbas Podracer all by itself in the Lost Pile at the resolution of the race, and regretted not waiting to Squabble until the next turn. I needed every differential point. At this point, something weird happens. Maul comes down on Captain Panaka and his Big Gat, and declares battle. I had completely forgotten the ability 3 thing, and apparently so had Josh. Maul cleaves the good Captain with his saber, and Panaka misses, because of The Phantom Menace. Whats that you say ? The Phantom Menace does not give the defense bonus unless there is a Jedi there ? You are right, but I forgot, and so did Josh, unfortunately. Dante Montoya was watching the game, and cringed when he saw the travesty. After a few turns of canceling Joshs drians with Senators and adding two to mine with Motion Supported, Josh could not hang on. Full win by 5. So end the day at 6 ( + 18 ), in second place behind Thomas Harris, who remained undefeated. Thomas of course chose to take the Maul foil, and the Qui-Gon foil would be given away at random. We all held our breath as Thomas drew a name from the pile of command cards. He flipped it over and read my name, so I ended up actually getting one of those foils. I opened my two packs of Coruscant I won for prize support, getting another Destroyer Droid and Something Stupid. I promptly traded the Destroyer Droid for another Might Of The Republic, for the next Type II event, where I WILL win the Darth Maul foil. In all, not a bad day. PROPS To Thomas Harris, for making a good show. Nice work, Thomas, but isnt FOUR The Phantom Menaces a little overboard ? To Brian Montez, for running a smooth event, as always. To Sebulba for finally learning how to drive. SLOPS To me and Josh for not paying attention. That game could have gone either way. To Podracing, because it is still dumb. To the Dark Side, for being much to powerful in the Type II environment. Maybe Theed Palace will change all of that. To Yoda, Depa, and Plo. You guys are supposed to be Jedi Masters, for The Makers sake ! Maul slapped you guys around like you were Nerf Herders.
